question: What three main areas come together to make up nursing informatics?

options.A: Nursing practice, hospital administration, and statistics
options.C: Nursing science, computer science, and information science

explanation: You've got this! Nursing informatics simply blends nursing knowledge with computer and information tools to help us handle health data smoothly. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is switching from paper to digital records so helpful in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: It makes doctors entirely responsible for patient record keeping
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for professional nurses
options.C: It ensures that patients never have to visit the hospital again
options.D: It helps reduce human error and secures patient health data

explanation: Great thinking! Moving to digital records helps cut down on mistakes and keeps patient information safe and easy to find. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h1)

question: In healthcare today, what does 'mHealth' stand for?
explanation: Spot on! mHealth simply means 'mobile health'—using phones and tablets to support patient care and health education. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h2)

question: A community health nurse in a remote Nigerian village needs to quickly figure out a children's drug dosage. What's the handiest tool to use?

options.B: A manual calculator with paper charts

explanation: Exactly! Having a calculator app right on your phone makes it super fast and easy to get accurate drug doses when you're out in the field. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the main job of wearable medical devices for patients?

options.C: Serving as a permanent surgical implant

explanation: You got it! Wearables like smart fitness or health bands are great for keeping an eye on vital signs over time without needing a hospital bed. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is a major headache nurses face when monitoring data from continuous wearable devices?

options.A: Inability of patients to charge their own phones
options.B: Alarm fatigue from frequent or false alerts
options.C: The physical weight of the wearable on the nurse
options.D: Patients refusing to remove the device ever

explanation: True story! When devices beep too often—even for minor things—nurses can become desensitized to the alerts, which is known as alarm fatigue. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the biggest plus of telehealth for patients living far away in rural areas?

options.A: Allowing patients to perform their own surgeries
options.C: Connecting them to specialist care without long travel
options.D: Eliminating the need for any prescription medications

explanation: Telehealth is a game-changer! It brings specialist doctors straight to rural patients, saving them long, exhausting, and expensive journeys. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h4)

question: A patient with heart failure lives three hours from the hospital. Which nursing action helps stop sudden readmissions?

options.A: Enrolling the patient in a remote patient monitoring program
options.B: Advising the patient to discard all weighing scales at home
options.C: Waiting until the patient develops severe edema to act
options.D: Instructing the patient to visit the clinic every single day

explanation: Brilliant choice! Remote monitoring lets us track daily changes like weight gain early, catching trouble before the patient ends up back in the hospital. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h4)

question: What does a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS) mainly do for healthcare workers?

options.C: Provide evidence-based recommendations using patient data
options.D: Take over all physical nursing care duties

explanation: Spot on! CDSS acts like a smart helper, giving you helpful prompts and evidence-based tips right when you're making clinical choices. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why must nurses still trust their own gut and assessment when looking at computer or AI recommendations?

options.A: AI outputs must be verified against direct patient assessment
options.B: Patients refuse to take medications suggested by a machine
options.C: Computers are always completely wrong about health conditions
options.D: Hospital management forbids the use of computer advice

explanation: Computers are great assistants, but you are the nurse! Always double-check digital advice against how the actual patient looks and feels. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h5)

question: What does 'interoperability' mean when talking about electronic health records?

options.A: Computers automatically print paper charts every morning
options.B: Doctors and nurses use completely separate filing cabinets
options.C: Only one hospital can access a patient's digital file
options.D: Different health systems can share data seamlessly

explanation: You got it! Interoperability just means different computer systems can easily talk to each other and share patient info without hitches. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h6)

question: How do Electronic Health Records (EHRs) make a nurse's daily shift easier?

options.A: By automatically discharging patients when they feel better
options.B: By centralizing patient data for quick access and reducing lost charts
options.C: By replacing all verbal communication between shift teams
options.D: By ensuring nurses never have to document patient care again

explanation: No more running around looking for lost folders! EHRs put all patient details in one neat, easy-to-reach digital spot. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common challenge when bringing new tech into Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: High financial cost of purchasing hardware
options.B: Excessive internet speed and constant power supply
options.C: Erratic and unreliable electrical power supply

explanation: Too true! Power cuts and slow internet are real hurdles we face, so 'excessive speed and constant power' is definitely not one of them. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h7)

question: What is a key duty for nurses when handling digital health records?

options.A: Protecting patient privacy and maintaining data security
options.B: Leaving computer screens unlocked at the nursing station
options.C: Publishing diagnostic results on social media platforms
options.D: Sharing patient passwords with everyone on the ward

explanation: Well done! Keeping patient records private and secure is a core professional duty that we must never compromise on. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T1#GNS113_U3_T1_h7)
